title: graphene oxide-boosted anaerobic co-fermentation of food waste and sewage sludge for volatile fatty acids production
description: The work investigates the effect of graphene oxide (GO) on the volatile fatty acids (VFAs) production in the co-fermentation system of food waste (FW) and sewage sludge (SS). A 35.4% enhancement in VFAs production is observed with GO, alongside a 26.5% increase in acetate production compared to the Control. The microbiota conducive to VFAs production (e.g., Bacteroides and Proteobacteria) is enriched. Metagenomics indicates the relative abundance of functional genes related to substrate hydrolysis (e.g., BglX and CLPP) and transport (e.g., gtsA, gltK, and gltI) and VFAs production (e.g., kor, pta, ackA and atoD) is upgraded by 3.5-29.2%, and functional genes (e.g., GLO1, gloB and pflD) associated with other products show a decrease of 4.7-20.8%, which underscores the metabolic regulatory of GO as RM, maintaining lower NADH favorable for VFAs production. This study provides a promising strategy for VFAs production through the stimulation of amino acid redox reactions, establishment of optimal IROS, and modulation of metabolic pathways in the anaerobic co-fermentation of FW and SS.
